info.name: Miqaat Core Identity Authorization
info.description:
## Tokens (no API keys)
Every request inherits `Bearer {{access_token}}`. Sign in with the *Miqaat Identity Federation* collection (folder **1. Sign in**): its select-scope requests store the globals `access_token` (audience authorization, CORE workspace) and `identity_access_token` (audience identity). Tokens last about 10 minutes; re-run select-scope on `401`.
Service-token folders need a single-use `client-authentication+jwt` signed by the calling principal (`federation_service_token`, `bu_service_token`).

## Run order for onboarding
Organisation → Applications → Roles & permissions → Clients (create, origins, callbacks, SECURITY_REVIEW, ACTIVE, Apply in Identity) → Users & assignments. Create requests store `tenant_id`, `bu_id`, `utility_id`, `role_id` and `client_id` for the requests after them.

## Status values
Clients: `PENDING → SECURITY_REVIEW → ACTIVE ⇄ SUSPENDED → RETIRED` (RETIRED is permanent). Tenants, business units, utilities, applications: `active` | `inactive`. Users: `active` | `inactive` | `suspended`. Roles have no status.

## Saved examples
Every request carries saved example responses (open a request → Examples): 204 in total, success and error. Each request description lists them under *Success responses* and *Error and edge-case responses*, with its purpose, when to use it and what it needs.
Sources: GET/denial examples captured from the running dev stack with a Business Unit Admin token; CORE administrator successes and edge cases captured from the isolated test database (miqaat_authz_test, same code, test data such as hbs-web-dev) so dev data was not changed. Tokens are redacted.
